_readme: Editorial pass over the generated stories. Principle: keep the researcher's
SWBST 'correct' line verbatim and bend the distractors to match its register
(subject form, infinitive form, length). 'correct' is only rewritten when it
was too long to read on a moving race card, and then only by trimming, never
by changing meaning. Where a page question is not SWBST-shaped, distractors
are rewritten to fit the SLOT rather than the question, since the race card
is answering the slot.
Card budget (P7): every race option -- correct and distractor alike -- must
fit 52 characters. The card is a fixed 1.55 x 0.85 world units with autosize
capped at 2.4 (F30) and is read while running; 52 is the widest option in the
playtested s01 stories. Cards are never enlarged to fit text; text is trimmed
to fit the card. flag.py is the gate.
QA pass 2026-08-05 -- READER OPTION LENGTH TELL.
F44 rebalanced the RACE cards (elements[].distractors) and left the Reader's own
question options untouched, even though the race distractors had been derived from
them. Measured across all 150 Reader questions: the correct option was strictly the
longest of the three in 124 (82.7%), mean +10.5 characters, max +37 -- so 'tap the
longest option' scored 81.3% against 33.3% for guessing. ReaderController shuffles
the three BUTTONS but not the three LENGTHS, and SessionLogService.OnPageAnswered
records the first answer per page into readingFirstCorrect, so that is study data.
Fix, following the same principle as F44: the researcher's correct option is never
touched; only distractors change, and they are EXTENDED rather than replaced, so an
already-false statement simply carries more (still false) detail. 111 distractors
across 74 questions -- 37 questions got both distractors pushed past the correct
option and 37 got one -- chosen as the 74 largest margins. Target: the correct
option's length rank spread evenly across longest/middle/shortest.
ALIGNMENT AUDIT 2026-08-06 -- PAGE <-> SLOT.
The instrument's whole design is a support-removal ladder: the Reader pre-teaches
SWBST slot k with the story text visible, the Race asks slot k with the text gone,
and the thesis wants a per-slot with-support / without-support contrast. Nothing in
the data or the code enforces the pairing -- there is no field linking a page
question to a slot, only the convention 'page k pre-teaches element k'. All 150
pairs were graded by hand: 135 aligned, 8 weak, 7 misaligned.
Two of the seven were OUR regressions (a P7 card-length trim that changed meaning)
and are restored to the researcher's own SWBST line: s04_easy BUT, s10_easy SO.
Five are misaligned in the researcher's SOURCE DOCUMENT, where the processing
question on page k asks about a different proposition than the SWBST line for slot k.
Those are repaired by rewriting the QUESTION toward the slot, never the SWBST line
(the SWBST analysis is the researcher's framework and the summary target). Every one
is a sign-off item, listed with the original question quoted in
Documentation/SummaRace_Story_Alignment_Audit.md.
s03_hard p2 is deliberately NOT fixed: its slot is the Giant's want, and page 2's
text carries no statement of it at all, so no faithful question can be written from
that page. It needs a researcher decision, not an invented question.
CARRYOVER PASS 2026-08-06 -- THE RACE WAS PASSABLE FROM MEMORY OF THE READER.
F44 closed the card-WIDTH tell and the 2026-08-05 pass closed the Reader's own
length tell, but nothing guarded the race's CORRECT card against the string the
Reader had just marked right for the same slot. Measured over all 150 slots:
'remember the Reader's answer for slot i, then take the race card most similar to
it' (difflib SequenceMatcher on normalised text, ties split) scored 83.7% against
33.3% for guessing, and 35.7-39.7% when deliberately misaligned to slot i+k -- so
the signal was slot-specific carried-over TEXT, not generic string similarity.
31 of 150 race correct lines were byte-identical to the Reader's taught answer
(6 of them outside SOMEBODY), and a pure memoriser earned 2-3 stars in 24 of the
30 stories. raceFirstPickCorrect IS the star count and the study's headline
measure, so a large part of what the race measured was 90-second verbatim recall.
Fix: reword the RACE 'correct' line so it states the same proposition in
different words from the Reader's answer. The proposition is never changed and
the Reader's questions are not touched (145/150 are the researcher's, verbatim);
every rewrite is grounded in its own page text and every one is listed for the
researcher's sign-off in Documentation/SummaRace_Carryover_Audit.md. Distractors
move only where a reworded correct line would otherwise breach flag.py's margins.
SOMEBODY IS EXEMPT AND MUST STAY THAT WAY. The Reader asks 'who is the story
about?' and the race asks the SOMEBODY slot; both answers are the character's
name, and there is no faithful paraphrase of a name. That slot scores 100% for a
memoriser before and after, and it is not a defect -- knowing who the story is
about IS the slot. The achievable floor for the whole corpus is therefore
After this pass: 60.3% overall, 50.4% outside SOMEBODY, 0 byte-identical pairs
outside SOMEBODY, 0 pairs where the Reader's answer is still CONTAINED in the
race card (was 37). The residual is SEMANTIC overlap -- the race card is about
the same idea the Reader taught, which is the support-removal ladder working as
designed. Do not chase it further by making a card mean something else.
Width bookkeeping after the carryover rewrite: reworded correct lines shifted
'correct is strictly the widest card' from 45.3% to 48.7%, so 19 distractors
were lengthened (same false claim, a little more detail) to bring it back under
the balanced 33.3% baseline rather than let F44's fix erode.
